problem: End-to-end navigation agents (RNN/Transformer over history, e.g. EmbCLIP) treat all past observations as equally associated, ignoring that navigation has only single-step direct causal links (O_t, a_t -> O_{t+1}). This can cause overfitting to spurious long-term correlations and slow, inefficient learning.
motivation: Unlike language, navigation has short-term dependencies: the next observation is determined by the current observation and action, and older history acts only indirectly through the current state. The authors therefore want to emphasize one-step causal associations without task-specific inductive biases or extra compute, so that the agent learns better environment understanding.
key_idea: Add an auxiliary next-observation-feature prediction loss (a causal loss, derived as a proxy for maximizing the conditional mutual information I(O_t; a_{t-1} | O_{t-1})) to a CLIP-based end-to-end transformer policy, so the one-step action-to-observation causation stands out.
insight: Most of the gain comes from the Causal Understanding Module rather than from the transformer. Removing it (Transformer) drops RoboTHOR ObjNav SR from 0.73 to 0.37, whereas swapping the transformer for an RNN (Causal-RNN) still keeps SR at 0.54 versus 0.42 for EmbCLIP. Causal-RNN reaches SR 0.48 in 15M steps, whereas EmbCLIP needs about 200M steps for 0.47, so the auxiliary loss also greatly speeds up training.
method: Visual Encoder: frozen CLIP ResNet-50 turns each observation into a feature z_i.
Text Embedding: simple Embedding layers map the objective and previous actions to features.
Causal Feature Integration: a tunable linear layer fuses the objective embedding with the CLIP visual features, giving a per-observation feature h_o_i (reflecting the O_t and Obj -> a_t assumption).

Multi-modal Transformer: single-layer, 4-head causal-masked transformer encoder over concatenated visual and action feature sequences; an Actor layer on the updated visual features predicts the action.

Causal Understanding Module: a linear probabilistic head predicts the Gaussian of the next visual feature from (o_t, a_t). The MI/KL objective reduces in practice to an MSE loss L_causal=E[(mu_theta - h_{v_{t+1}})^2].
Training: PPO with total objective L_PPO - alpha*L_causal (alpha=1), 100M steps, Adam lr 1e-4 with linear decay, AllenAct, episode length 128; the best-SR checkpoint is selected.
Supervised transfer: the same module is plugged into Seq2Seq, Speaker-Follower and EnvDrop on R2R with other settings unchanged.

setting.backbone: Frozen CLIP ResNet-50 visual encoder + single-layer transformer encoder (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: RL in simulator for 100M steps per task (RoboTHOR ObjNav, Habitat MP3D ObjNav, Gibson PointNav); no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (CLIP features); PointNav additionally uses polar goal coordinates
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (MoveAhead, Rotate L/R, LookUp/Down for RoboTHOR; Stop/Done)

results: CAN clearly beats the EmbCLIP baseline under identical setups: RoboTHOR ObjNav SR 0.73 vs 0.42, Habitat ObjNav SR 0.39 vs 0.16, PointNav SPL 0.93 vs 0.84. It also edges the leaderboard entries reported, such as ProcTHOR (SR 0.66) and RIM (SR 0.37). Adding the module to Seq2Seq, Speaker-Follower and EnvDrop on R2R val-unseen raises SR by 16-20 points.
limitations: The causal assumptions (single-step direct causation, Gaussian next-feature prediction) are idealized; the practical loss is just next-feature MSE, close to existing auxiliary prediction and curiosity ideas.

Evaluation is limited to simple benchmarks with a small 1-layer model and no strong VLN or large-scale comparisons; the R2R gains are reported only on weak/old baselines, and the leaderboard comparisons are not like-for-like.
Splits and benchmark details are under-specified; the mutual-information derivation relies on loose bound approximations.
